transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-09
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lee (Moonstone VP Eng), Marta (Cloud Architect), Omar (Security), Yvonne (DevOps)
Shared artifacts: 'Moonstone connectivity spreadsheet', 'Redwood private endpoints primer link', 'security questionnaire (redwood-sq-2027.pdf)'

Summary: quick discovery to map Moonstone's multi-account VPC footprint, discuss express/onramp options (ExpressRoute/DirectConnect), private endpoints vs peering, egress controls per region, and pilot sizing. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private but leaning to private VPC because of regulatory and data residency constraints.

[00:00] Jared: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm jared kim from redwood, i run the ae motion on infra customers. can you hear me ok?
[00:08] Lee: yep loud and clear, thanks jared, yeah im lee, vp eng at moonstone. we have like a fairly spread out vpc estate across three clouds and we're trying to figure out the least disruptive way to bring redwood into our private network.
[00:17] Priya: hi all, priya nair, solutions engineer. i'll dig into the networking and latency/cost tradeoffs. quick ask — can you confirm where your control plane needs to sit and which regions are allowed for data residency?
[00:29] Marta: sure, main constraints: EU data must stay in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for now, and we have a regulatory requirement that PII never leave those regions. us-east-1 is ok for non-prod.
[00:39] Omar: and security wants all keys in our KMS and audit logs forwarded to our splunk tenant, so a private deployment would be preferred.
[00:46] Yvonne: hi team, we'll likely handle the VPC peering and transit work — we use Azure ExpressRoute for a lot of onprem traffic, but we also have AWS DirectConnect for some services, so hybrid.
[00:57] Jared: ok good context. two high-level approaches we see: 1) Redwood Private deployed into your VPCs with private endpoints and private link style access, or 2) Dedicated in a customer-managed VPC with our control plane in a restricted region. the tradeoffs are latency and operational effort.
[01:13] Lee: curious about the private endpoints option — does that require per-account peering or can we centralize via a transit?
[01:19] Priya: good question. we typically support both: you can use transit gateway peering and share private endpoints from a central connectivity VPC, or use per-account interface endpoints. for Azure the pattern maps to Private Link + Private Endpoint, and for AWS it's interface VPC endpoints behind TGW.
[01:33] Marta: ptcl note: we already have a transit hub in eu-central, don't want to change routing too much. would prefer the central VPC model.
[01:40] Omar: any egress implications? we need to control outbound to specific regions and monitor tokens leaving.
[01:46] Priya: yes; egress is controlled by where the inference runtime runs. if you pin models to eu regions, traffic stays local. for our Dedicated/Private deployments we can guarantee runtime in the allowed regions and block egress to other regions via security groups and route tables. small caveat — any external billing telemetry to our hosted control plane will transit; we can arrange private peering for that as well.
[02:05] Yvonne: oh ok, so the control plane talk — we want the control plane either inside our VPC or talk over a private link; we can't have management plane traffic over the public internet.
[02:13] Jared: totally, customers often want private control plane connectivity. we offer a customer-managed control plane that can sit behind private endpoints or talk over ExpressRoute/DirectConnect — it depends on the network topology.
[02:24] Lee: does Redwood require any special IP ranges? we've got overlapping RFC1918 ranges across accounts, so NAT or translation is a pain.
[02:31] Priya: we don't require specific IPs but our private endpoints need routable IPs inside the peered space. If you have overlapping CIDRs, the usual approach is to put the endpoints in a hub VPC and use NAT/gateway translation or route53 private hosted zones with conditional forwarding. we can show two patterns in the diagram.
[02:47] Marta: can you briefly explain the pilot sizing? we're concerned about latency for chat workloads.
[02:52] Priya: for chat with 512 tokens avg and a small MPT-style open model, overhead is mainly seq-latency and GPU travel. for a pilot we'd recommend a small dedicated pool in eu-central with autoscale burst — maybe 2 x A10 equivalent to mimic your p95 and then ramp. for private we can spin up on-prem or in customer VPC GPUs; for Hosted there's more network hop if not colocated.
[03:14] Omar: and encryption, we want HSM-backed keys. does Redwood integrate KMS/HSM?
[03:19] Jared: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault and support HSM via partner integrations — we'll attach the SOC2 and HSM notes after this call.
[03:26] Lee: i'm hearing both express route and private link options, do you have a recommendation given we use ExpressRoute extensively for onprem -> azure?
[03:34] Priya: if most traffic originates from Azure and you have ExpressRoute, mapping control plane to Private Link and using peered private endpoints over ExpressRoute gives the lowest hop count. for cross-cloud you're likely to centralize via TGW/VWAN and expose interface endpoints to the hub.
[03:49] Yvonne: there's one tricky bit — our firewall blocks unknown egress IP ranges, so we need a fixed egress IP for the outbound traffic to Redwood services. can you provide stable egress IPs?
[03:58] Jared: for hosted we publish an egress IP block list, but for private/dedicated deployments we can allocate fixed elastic IPs in your account or you can route via NAT in the hub VPC to provide stable addresses.
[04:11] Marta: will the model weights ever go to an external store? our concern is data residency but also model snapshot handling.
[04:18] Priya: model weights are stored in whatever storage you designate for private deployments; we can keep them in a customer-managed blob bucket with SSE-KMS. for hosted models we host weights but can offer dedicated tenancy. we'll note the weights residency in the security doc.
[04:32] Lee: any limitations on throughput for private endpoints? we've seen some customers hit throttling with interface endpoints at high TPS.
[04:39] Priya: good callout. interface endpoints have per-ENI throughput limits per cloud provider; our recommended pattern for high throughput is to use multiple endpoints per AZ and load balancing or deploy the runtime inside the same VPC to avoid endpoint throttles. we also do batching to improve tokens/sec.
[04:56] Omar: about logging — can we forward inference logs and audit trails to our splunk via an endpoint?
[05:02] Jared: yes, we can push logs to your syslog/splunk ingestion over a private peered path or forward via a customer-managed ingestion queue. we also support kafka/stream exports inside the VPC.
[05:12] Lee: curious, what's the expected time to stand up a private pilot? we want minimal downtime.
[05:17] Priya: typical pilot for private with two regions is 2-4 weeks: network config and private endpoint provisioning 3-7 days, provision GPUs and runtime 2-5 days, QA and load tests 3-7 days. depends on firewall and procurement.
[05:31] Marta: procurement might take longer. also, cost questions — we need a crisp E2E cost slide: what is the cost delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[05:39] Jared: we'll send a cost estimator, but in general: hosted is lowest operational burden, dedicated reduces per-token unit cost at scale, and private has additional infra overhead (VPC, egress NAT, storage) but gives compliance guarantees. we can run a cost model for your 1000 concurrent user baseline.
[05:58] Yvonne: network question: will we need to open ports inbound to our workloads for control signals?
[06:03] Priya: inbound is minimal — mostly control plane reachability from Redwood to your control endpoints; for private setups we prefer mutual TLS over the private peering so you dont open public ports.
[06:13] [CROSSTALK] Omar: (inaudible) — if the control plane is inside our VPC, who maintains it?
[06:17] Jared: if it's customer-managed control plane, you will host the control plane in your account and we provide the deployment manifests and handle the application-level updates under agreed maintenance windows.
[06:28] Lee: ok good. there was a mention earlier about prefix/KV cache being shared across tenants — can you clarify caching in private deployments?
[06:36] Priya: in private/dedicated deployments your KV cache lives in the runtime in your VPC and isn't shared. hosted multi-tenant caches are logically isolated but some metadata may be pooled; for strict isolation we recommend private.
[06:48] Marta: do you support regional model variants or quantized models for cost saving?
[06:53] Priya: yes we have model catalog with verified quantized builds; you can pin a quantized variant per route. that saves GPU memory and cost but can slightly affect quality; we'll run evals on your prompts.
[07:06] Omar: for regulatory audits, do you provide log retention and immutable audit exports?
[07:11] Jared: yes, we can retain logs for a configurable retention period and provide immutable export snapshots to your storage. we'll include a sample retention policy and how to pull exports.
[07:21] Lee: any pitfalls you've seen with ExpressRoute/VWAN + TGW mixing?
[07:25] Priya: yes route propagation conflicts sometimes cause asymmetric routing which breaks private endpoints; solution is explicit route tables on the hub and source/dest checks. also verify MTU across ExpressRoute. we'll add a checklist.
[07:38] Yvonne: oh — MTU. last time we had fragmentation issues with model payloads. important to call out.
[07:43] Priya: noted.
[07:45] [00:45] Jared: quick pause — i'm jotting the key constraints: region residency, KMS/HSM, stable egress IPs, central hub VPC pref, avoid CIDR overlap issues. anything missing?
[07:58] Marta: SLA expectations — we need 99.9 latency SLO at p95 for inference for prod.
[08:04] Priya: we offer SLOs and can map them in dedicated capacity contracts. for private we'll include latency guarantees in the runbook and provide tracing hooks.
[08:13] Omar: security question — vulnerability scanning on the runtime images?
[08:18] Priya: we run automated image scans and can share SBOMs. we also support signed images via your registry.
[08:27] Lee: ok let's talk next steps and a timeline. we want a pilot in eu-central and eu-west in the next four weeks if possible. procurement is aggressive.
[08:36] Jared: action plan: 1) we'll send a connectivity diagram with 2 architecture options (hub-VPC private endpoints and per-account interface endpoints), 2) send SOC2, HSM integration notes and SBOM process, 3) propose pilot configuration and cost estimate.
[08:48] Marta: on the diagram, please include port numbers and firewall rules.
[08:52] Priya: absolutely, we'll include a port matrix.
[08:55] Yvonne: and can you provide a sample terraform snippet for the endpoints?
[08:59] Priya: yes, we'll attach a terraform module example for both AWS and Azure.
[09:04] Omar: pm question — how do you handle model rollouts and canary behavior inside a private deployment?
[09:10] Priya: we support canary and A/B rollouts at the route level. for private deployments we can map different model versions to different runtime pools and route traffic via weighted routing. automatic fallback to a smaller model is also configurable.
[09:24] Lee: are there any licensing blockers for bringing third-party models into our private infra?
[09:29] Jared: licensing depends on the model; we have guidance and can help with open model compliance. if commercial license is needed we supply the procurement touchpoints.
[09:38] Marta: one last network nit: do you support AWS PrivateLink across accounts with cross-account principals? we have org accounts.
[09:45] Priya: yes, cross-account interface endpoints are a supported pattern; we can also use endpoint services and authorize principals. we'll document the terraform IAM snippets.
[09:55] [09:55] Lee: ok, i'm going to recap for my team: we'll review the connectivity spreadsheet, share our allowed CIDRs and region list, and confirm procurement timeline by friday.
[10:05] Jared: great. i'll follow up with the docs and the diagrams. thanks all for your time.

Recap & Next steps (verbatim):
- Redwood to send connectivity diagram (hub vs per-account), port matrix and terraform examples.
- Redwood to send SOC2, HSM/KMS notes, SBOM and security questionnaire link.
- Moonstone to confirm region list, CIDR ranges and any regulatory docs.
- Schedule a follow-up deep-dive with Moonstone networking team next week (Jared to send invite).

End of transcript.
